item.title: Trowels to Terabytes: Accessibility and Re-use of Heritage Data at the Archaeology Data Service
item.description:
Nicky Garland
The Archaeology Data Service is the leading digital repository for archaeology and heritage in the UK. The core activity of the ADS is the long-term digital preservation of the data entrusted to our care — a vital undertaking for the heritage sector — and its dissemination in accordance with the FAIR data principles. We achieve this through precise standards and metadata schemas that ensure findability and interoperability, and through open, accessible collections that maximise reuse by others.

item.title: YouTube Recommendations Content Access and Prospective Prediction
item.description:
Jessica Schmidt
This companion protocol examines recommendation feedback, differences between content access routes and claims of apparent prediction. It specifies prospective records, fixed scoring and baseline comparisons. The source conversations document the research questions; no controlled recommendation experiment or completed prediction series is reported. The case can be investigated independently while preserving its methodological connection to the computational loops audit.
